scope: First three primary legal-rule packets; statutory values are not legislative selectable bounds or causal ranges.

entries.rule: Complaint-warrant indictable/disorderly-persons cases, subject to exceptions; nonmonetary release prioritized. Money permitted only if other conditions cannot reasonably assure appearance. Detention requires prosecutor motion and clear-and-convincing statutory findings.
entries.currentLawLimit: Original enacted 2014 statute; 2026 amendments not verified. No categorical no-money or violent-only detention claim.

selectableRange.missing: Current higher-level legal limits and operative amendments; existing statute is not a proposed-law min/max.

entries.sourceVersion: Compiler footer 11/29/2022; subsequent amendments not verified
entries.ageBasis: Ordinary juvenile violation jurisdiction uses age when proceedings commence; transfer provisions use age at offense.
entries.transfer: Age16+ first/second-degree felony automatically adult, including related scheme charges; age16+ misdemeanor/third-degree felony discretionary certification after investigation; under16 homicide discretionary certification after investigation. Traffic exception also applies.

selectableRange.missing: Current amendments and higher-level constraints on proposed age;18 is a statutory starting value, not a selectable interval.

entries.rule: Voting exclusion is incarceration under a sentence of imprisonment. Removal of that exclusion does not itself register the person or cast a ballot; citizenship, age, residency, registration and other statutory eligibility remain.
entries.restorationEvent: No longer incarcerated under sentence; not generic completion of all probation/parole obligations.
entries.registration: Cancellation may follow certification of confinement; actual registration status must be read and restored through the registration writer.

selectableRange.missing: Current consolidated law/higher-level constraints on proposed exclusion categories; no invented numerical range.

runtimeProof: Pretrial saved-consequence attribution tested separately. These three jurisdiction-specific rule packets are not nationwide runtime proof.
